name: Og
description: King living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness

points: Moses gave unto the children of Gad and of Reuben and unto half the tribe of Manasseh the kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorites and the kingdom of Og king of Bashan, the land with the cities thereof, and they built their cities and folds for sheep.

note.label: Numbers 32: The Inheritance of Reuben and Gad on This Side Jordan

points: Only Og king of Bashan remained of the remnant of giants. His bedstead was a bedstead of iron, nine cubits long and four cubits broad: about thirteen feet long and six feet wide, near the size of two king beds, showing how tall and big this man was.

note.label: Deuteronomy 3: The Battle Is the Lord's

points: All the region of Argob with all Bashan was called the land of giants, because the giants there were of Og's kin, of his family.

note.label: Deuteronomy 3: The Battle Is the Lord's

points: Sihon king of Heshbon and Og king of Bashan came out against Israel, and Israel smote them and gave their land for an inheritance to the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half tribe of Manasseh.

note.label: Deuteronomy 29: The Covenant Made with Us Who Were Not There

points: For we have heard how the Lord dried up the water of the Red sea for you. We heard what your God did to the Egyptians, who were a great and powerful kingdom. When ye came out of Egypt; and what ye did unto the two kings of the Amorites, that were on the other side Jordan, Sihon and Og, whom ye utterly destroyed. We saw your God destroy kings, dry up the Red Sea, kill the firstborn of the Egyptians. We know that you have got a real God.

Her faith came by report: we have heard how the Lord dried up the water of the Red Sea for you, and what ye did unto Sihon and Og, the two kings of the Amorites whom ye utterly destroyed; and as soon as we had heard it, our hearts did melt, neither did there remain any more courage in any man. The Lord had said he would put that spirit on the nations.
The Gibeonites leaned on the fame of the Most High: we have heard all that he did in Egypt, and to Sihon king of Heshbon and Og king of Bashan, the two kings of the Amorites beyond Jordan.

note.label: Joshua 9: The Gibeonite Deception and the Weight of an Oath

points: The Reubenites and the Gadites had already received their inheritance with the half tribe of Manasseh, which Moses gave them beyond Jordan eastward: all the cities of Sihon king of the Amorites and all the kingdom of Og in Bashan, who remained of the remnant of the giants, for these did Moses smite and cast out.

note.label: Joshua 13: Much Land Yet to Be Possessed

points: Moses gave inheritance unto the half tribe of Manasseh by their families: from Mahanaim, all Bashan, all the kingdom of Og, and all the towns of Jair, threescore cities, pertaining unto the children of Machir the son of Manasseh.

note.label: Joshua 13: Much Land Yet to Be Possessed

cases.name: Sihon and Og
cases.charge: Refusing Israel passage on the king’s highway and coming out to battle against them
cases.preview: Israel was forbidden to meddle with Esau, Moab or Ammon, for the Most High had appointed their possessions.
